subject: Next steps: DataForge latency/throughput benchmark scope & timeline
messages:
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@dataforge.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@dataforge.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — next steps on latency/throughput bench

Tessa — thanks again for the walkthrough today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can prioritize the POC: 

- Goal: narrow decision between Redwood and the two hyperscaler-managed inference endpoints (HypCloud + GoliathAI) for our conversational assistant (10k token context, ~10 q/s steady, bursty daytime traffic).
- Key metrics we care about: p95 and p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (steady-state and peak bursts), cold vs warm cache behavior, model output parity (sanity checks), and sustained throughput over 30min windows.

As discussed, we'd like Redwood to run an A/B bench with:
1) base model variant (your recommended open LLM comparable to HypCloud’s managed 13B)
2) quantized variant (8-bit or whatever you recommend)
3) a fallback smaller model for tail-latency mitigation

Please include an explicit test matrix (payload sizes, concurrency, warmup steps) and an estimate for how long the run takes, plus any infra prerequisites (VPC peering, ingest keys, allowed IPs). We're aiming for an internal decision by Oct 25; ideally we get results by Oct 20 so our engs can validate.

Also please share a rough SOW and any cost estimates for running the dedicated bench.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick sync later this week if helpful.

—Jamie
Jamie Lee
Director of Platform Engineering, DataForge
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@dataforge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps on latency/throughput bench

Jamie — really appreciate the clear call notes. Copying Marcus (bench lead) and Jordan (solutions) so they can scope the test matrix and timings. Action items from Redwood: 

- Marcus to propose a concrete A/B test matrix (p95/p99, tokens/sec, cold/warm, payloads) + an estimated runtime.
- Redwood to share a draft SOW and a one-page cost estimate for the lab runs (including any dedicated capacity costs).
- Logistics: we need a list of sample prompts (we can use a redacted set if you prefer), IP allowlist, and preferred time window for a 3-hour run (we recommend an overnight window to avoid daytime noise, but will accommodate).

Attachments I’ll include now: a starter test-matrix CSV and our internal runbook template. Marcus — can you review the matrix and add concrete commands and warmup sequence? Jordan — can you prepare a short slide for Oct 19 internal review (if DataForge wants to present the outputs)?

I'll set a calendar for a short checkpoint on Oct 14. If you want the results by Oct 20, Marcus will need signoff on the matrix by Oct 13 EOD.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@dataforge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Thanks — next steps on latency/throughput bench

Thanks — I drafted a concrete test plan below. High level: we run three A/B arms (Redwood-default, Redwood-quant, Redwood-fallback) against HypCloud and GoliathAI baselines using the same payloads. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and per-request token costs.

Test matrix (summary):
- Context lengths: 512, 2048, 4096, 10k (synthetic but representative).
- Concurrency profile: 1, 5, 10, 25 virtual users (to simulate steady and small bursts).
- Payloads: 8 prompt templates (you provide 4; we will redact and augment).
- Warmup: sequential single-user warmup for 3 minutes per model to populate KV cache; then steady load ramp for 5 minutes.
- Run duration: 30 minutes per bucket for steady-state metrics; we recommend two repeats (n=2) for variance estimate.
- Metrics collected: p50, p95, p99 latencies (ms), tokens/sec (aggregate and per-second), tail drop/failures, CPU/GPU utilization, and detailed traces (if you enable trace-ids).

Operational notes and commands (high-level):
1) Redwood will expose an ephemeral endpoint for the run; we will provide a short-lived API key valid for the lab window.
2) We will provide a run script (bench-run.sh) that uses vegeta/locust harness to drive the traffic. Example payload: POST /v1/generate with n_ctx header and streaming disabled for consistent wall-clock measurement.
3) Cold vs Warm: we will run each config with a cold start (no warmup) then the warmup-run to show delta.
4) KV caching: for the 10k context we will use a 5-minute prefix warmup to populate KV and measure autocomplete.

Estimated time: end-to-end (matrix finalization, infra prep, runs, analysis) = 6 business days after signoff. If you sign off by Oct 13 EOD, we can deliver results by Oct 20.

Attachments: dataforge-bench-matrix.csv (test bucket details), redwood-benchmark-runbook.md (run steps + scripts), sow-draft-dataforge.pdf (SOW draft with optional dedicated capacity pricing).

Questions for DataForge:
- Can you confirm the 4 sample prompt templates and whether redaction is acceptable?
- Do you need results to include per-token cost modeled for HypCloud/Goliath? We can provide a best-effort cost comparison but will need their published unit prices.
- Any compliance constraints (e.g., IP allowlists, VPC peering) we should plan for?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@dataforge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@dataforge.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps on latency/throughput bench

Marcus/Tessa — this looks excellent and thorough, thank you. Confirming:
- We will provide 4 redacted prompt templates by Oct 12 5pm PT.
- We can sign off on the matrix by Oct 13 EOD.
- IP allowlist: will send our CIDR ranges and ask security to enable the ephemeral key window.
- One additional ask: can you include correlation ids (X-DF-Trace) in the logs and a small sample of per-request trace payloads (we'll share a schema)? That will help our SREs validate end-to-end observability.

If everything proceeds we expect to make a vendor decision by Oct 25. Please go ahead with the prep and send the SOW + cost estimate; Samir will review the commercials.

—Jamie
